meta_description: Old Baldy in Austin, the oak Sam Houston camped under at Gonzales and the live oaks Kennedy's motorcade passed. {trees} Texas trees across {places} places.
intro: Texas remembers its trees by who stood under them. A Franciscan priest wrote about Austin's Old Baldy cypress in 1716. Sam Houston camped beside a Dallas bur oak in 1843 and slept under a live oak at Gonzales with the town burning behind him. Austin's first city lots were auctioned in 1839 in the shade of oaks that still stand on a downtown square, and the Treaty Oak survived a man pouring enough herbicide round its roots in 1989 to kill a hundred trees. The state also keeps a champion register, so beside the famous oaks stand trees that are simply the biggest of their kind anywhere in Texas: a mesquite ranchers would bulldoze, a jujube by a Fort Worth road, a yaupon most of the South clips into a hedge. Live oaks dominate, and they grow wider than they grow tall.
